clue.text: Wine companion knocked back one over the eight with top chef

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for Companion of Honour

indicators.note: a drink knocked back goes down in one; here the word for one over the eight is turned round

parts.note: one more than eight is nine (the phrase usually means a drink too many)
Raymond Blanc is a celebrated French-born chef working in Britain

explanation.surface: A drinker downs one glass too many in the company of a famous chef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' turns NINE into ENIN. 'One over the eight' is British slang for being slightly drunk, which hides its literal sense of nine.
explanation.definitionFit: Chenin blanc is a white grape variety and the white wine made from it.

clue.text: As Parisian, start to recognise rising city traffic

parts.note: comme is French for 'as', so a Parisian would say it

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, taken here from recognise
in a down clue, rising means the letters for city are read upwards

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London

explanation.surface: A Parisian begins to notice the traffic building up in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns EC into CE at the foot of the down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic as a noun means trade or dealing, a synonym of commerce.

clue.text: In final speech, low-class cheek's conjured up by rascal, right to be rejected

parts.note: E is the lowest social grade in British market-research classification

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for cheek is read from bottom to top

parts.note: lip means impudence or cheek

indicators.note: rejected means the letter for right is thrown out of the word for rascal

parts.note: a rogue is a rascal

explanation.surface: A closing address mocks a cheeky lower-class rascal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conjured up' turns LIP into PIL; 'to be rejected' takes R from ROGUE to leave OGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: An epilogue is the closing speech of a play, addressed to the audience.

clue.text: Frostiness rearing in old Brits

parts.note: ice is frost, coldness

indicators.note: in a down clue, rearing up means the little word in is read upwards

explanation.surface: A chilly reception rises among ancient Britons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rearing' turns IN into NI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were a tribe of ancient Britain, led by Boudicca against Rome.

clue.text: I can't ramble alongside unpleasant smell of plants

indicators.note: alongside places the smell next to the rearranged letters, ahead of them in the answer

parts.note: BO is body odour

indicators.note: to ramble is to wander aimlessly, so the letters of I can't are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone can't go for a walk because of the stink from the plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ramble' rearranges I CANT into TANIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanic is an adjective meaning relating to plants or botany.

clue.text: Growing every year, adult avoided American doughnut say

indicators.note: something avoided is left out, so the letter for adult is dropped

parts.note: a plant growing every year, or yearly, is annual
A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: An American adult steers clear of the doughnuts that are getting bigger each year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoided' drops the A from ANNUAL to leave ANNUL.
explanation.definitionFit: An annulus is a ring-shaped figure, and a doughnut is an everyday example of that shape.

clue.text: She predicted when hospital doctor would settle in California

indicators.note: settling in means the pieces take up residence inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
san is short for sanatorium, a kind of hospital

explanation.surface: A seer foretold when a hospital doctor would move to California.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassandra, in Greek legend, prophesied truly but was never believed.

clue.text: Head of Wimbledon circles court

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here taken from Wimbledon

parts.note: two circles look like the letters O and O

explanation.surface: The Wimbledon chief walks round a tennis court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' is the verb, to pay romantic attention, not a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: To court someone is to woo them, seeking their affection.

clue.text: Fish out of water? It's caught here possibly by cook

parts.note: fish may be caught at a weir, a small river dam
to do food is to cook it

explanation.surface: A stranded fish might be caught at a dam and then cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish out of water' looks literal but is the idiom for a misfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish out of water is a person who seems odd and out of place, a weirdo.

clue.text: T-shirts seen centrally in unit, available temporarily

indicators.note: in places the middle letters of the shirts inside the word for unit

parts.note: one is a single unit

indicators.note: centrally points to the central letters of the word T-shirts

explanation.surface: T-shirts in one shop can be had for a short while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen centrally' takes HIR, the middle three letters of TSHIRTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on hire can be rented for a period rather than bought.

clue.text: Some of US drama in evening partly missed

indicators.note: parts of the outer words are left out, so the answer sits inside drama in evening

explanation.surface: Part of an American drama was missed in the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Maine is one of the states making up the United States.

clue.text: Songwriter's fan recalled times when touring hard

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word for fan is read in reverse

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast or fan

indicators.note: touring means moving around, so the letters of times are mixed

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A songwriter's fan remembers times on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns NUT into TUN; 'when touring' rearranges TIMES into ESMIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunesmith is an informal word for a composer of popular songs.

clue.text: Sentimental book about Loch on Scottish island

indicators.note: on means the loch's letter is added to the island
about means turned round, so the word for book is reversed

parts.note: a tome is a large book
Iona is an island of the Inner Hebrides
L is the map abbreviation for loch

explanation.surface: A sentimental book about a loch on a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns TOME into EMOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotional and sentimental both describe being moved by feeling.

clue.text: Tree snake, left for dead at first

indicators.note: for means one letter stands in place of another

parts.note: an adder is a venomous snake

indicators.note: the first letter of dead is the one swapped out

explanation.surface: A snake in a tree is left for dead.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the first D of ADDER for L gives the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The alder is a tree of the birch family that grows by water.

clue.text: Soap maker from Australia twitches nervously during concluding part

indicators.note: during places the pieces within the word for concluding part

parts.note: a coda is the concluding section of a piece of music
tics are nervous twitches

explanation.surface: An Australian soap producer twitches nervously during the finale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soap maker' suggests a TV soap producer; it is the chemical used in making soap.
explanation.definitionFit: Caustic soda, sodium hydroxide, reacts with fats to make soap.

clue.text: Artist whose work is barely shown?

definitions.text: Artist whose work is barely shown?

parts.words: Artist whose work is barely shown?
parts.note: barely shown reads as hardly displayed, but means shown on bare skin, where this artist's designs appear

explanation.surface: An artist whose work hardly ever gets exhibited.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattooist inks designs into the skin, so the work is seen on bare flesh.

clue.text: See 13
Volcanic glass is picked up by investigator in Scottish town

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the name of the town

parts.note: Oban is a port town in Argyll, western Scotland

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means the word is is lifted and read upwards

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A detective in a Scottish town picks up a piece of volcanic glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' turns IS into SI.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsidian is a dark glassy rock formed when lava cools rapidly.

clue.text: Mohave shows this small equine, describing journey around north

indicators.note: describing in its sense of drawing round means the equine encloses the rest

parts.note: an ass is a small member of the horse family

indicators.note: around means the word for journey wraps the letter for north

parts.note: a ride is a journey

explanation.surface: In the Mohave, a donkey sets off on a trip northwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mohave is a desert, and dryness or aridness is what a desert displays.

clue.text: Group of ministers stiffen tone

parts.note: to starch fabric is to stiffen it
amber is a colour tone, a yellowish orange

explanation.surface: A cabinet hardens its tone.
explanation.definitionFit: The Star Chamber was an English court of the king's councillors, and the term now means any secretive body of ministers.

clue.text: Fruit rot

definitions.meaning: the pink stalks of this plant are cooked and eaten as a fruit
rot here means nonsense or empty talk

explanation.definitionFit: Rhubarb is eaten like a fruit, and also means nonsense, from actors murmuring it as background noise.

clue.text: See 18
TV presenter, hard to miss, who's chewing over programme's finale

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first part on top of the last letter
missing means the letter for hard is left out

parts.note: a chomper is one who chews noisily
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: the finale of a word is its last letter, taken from programme's

explanation.surface: A TV host, hard to overlook, chews over the end of the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to miss' removes H from CHOMPER, leaving COMPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A compere is the host who introduces acts on a television or stage show.

clue.text: Talk frantically, extremely drained, as one's hard pressed at the desk?

definitions.text: one's hard pressed at the desk?

indicators.note: frantically means in a wild flurry, so the letters of Talk are jumbled
only the extreme letters are kept, the inner ones dropped from the word for drained

parts.note: something drained is empty

explanation.surface: Someone talks wildly, exhausted, hard-pressed at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frantically' rearranges TALK into ALTK; 'extremely' keeps only the end letters of EMPTY, giving EY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alt key is a computer keyboard key, held down firmly while typing at a desk.

clue.text: Drug crime involving cheap items

indicators.note: involving means the word for crime wraps round the other piece

parts.note: a sin is a wrongdoing, a crime
tat is cheap, shoddy goods

explanation.surface: A drug offence involving cheap tat.
explanation.definitionFit: A statin is a cholesterol-lowering drug.

clue.text: Draw time after time in little room

indicators.note: in places the two letters inside the word for little room

parts.note: the loo is the lavatory, the smallest room

indicators.note: after sets one letter for time behind another

explanation.surface: Someone keeps drawing in a small room, time and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' is the noun, a prize draw, not sketching.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a lottery game in which numbers are drawn.

clue.text: Single university memory returned when in diner, wandering

indicators.note: in places the reversed memory inside the jumbled letters
wandering means straying, so the letters of diner are jumbled
returned means sent back, so the word for memory is read backwards

parts.note: RAM is computer memory

explanation.surface: A single student recalls memories while wandering in a diner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single' looks like part of the surface's student but is the definition; the reversed memory sits after the first letter of the jumbled diner.
explanation.definitionFit: Single and unmarried both describe a person without a spouse.

clue.text: Are you texting a letter to get money abroad?

parts.note: in text-speak, 'are you' is written R U
pee is the spelt-out name of the letter P

explanation.surface: Someone texting asks whether you will send a letter for cash overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: The rupee is the currency of India and several other countries.

clue.text: Bird supplies new technology around festival

parts.note: kit is equipment or supplies

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the technology abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: IT, information technology, is the modern tech field
a wake is a local festival or holiday in northern England

explanation.surface: A bird brings tech gear to a festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' signals the reversal of the technology letters. A wake is a northern English holiday festival.
explanation.definitionFit: The kittiwake is a small gull of the open sea.

clue.text: Some cats curiously examined via the mouth

indicators.note: spoken via the mouth means the word is judged by how it is pronounced

parts.note: to pry is to look curiously, and pried is its past tense

explanation.surface: Some cats were inspected by looking into their mouths.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of lions is a pride, so a pride is some big cats.

clue.text: That Scottish play's ultimate character performing

indicators.note: the ultimate character of a word is its last letter, here from play's

parts.note: an actor performing is on stage, on

explanation.surface: The last character to appear in the Scottish play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scottish play' calls up Macbeth, but 'That Scottish' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Yon is a Scottish and dialect word for that or yonder.

clue.text: Olympic athlete appears on computer game

indicators.note: appears on puts the athlete's name next to the computer in the answer

parts.note: a tablet is a portable touchscreen computer
Jessica Ennis is a British heptathlete, Olympic champion in 2012

explanation.surface: An Olympic athlete features in a computer game.
explanation.definitionFit: Table tennis, or ping-pong, is a bat-and-ball game, itself an Olympic sport.
